name: RT-2 (Vision-Language-Action Models, Brohan et al. 2023)
observations: Core thesis: instead of building a VLM-plus-planner-plus-controller stack, co-fine-tune a large pretrained VLM directly on robot trajectories so a single end-to-end network maps camera images + text instruction to low-level actions. RT-2 belongs to the class named Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

Key technical trick: represent actions as text. The action vector is 6-DoF end-effector delta position and rotation + gripper extension + a discrete terminate command; each continuous dimension is discretized into 256 uniform bins, giving 8 integers serialized as one space-separated string (e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'). No new parameters or action-only heads are added, so weights are entirely shared between language and action tasks.

Action-token binding depends on the backbone tokenizer: for PaLI-X, integers 0-1000 already have unique tokens so bins map to existing integer tokens; for PaLM-E, the 256 least-frequently-used tokens are overwritten to form the action vocabulary (a form of symbol tuning).

I/O format: input is VQA-style ('Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:'), images come from the robot camera; output is the action string. Training objective is plain next-token prediction, which is equivalent to behavior-cloning loss in robot learning.

Co-fine-tuning is the critical recipe detail: keep the original web vision-language data (VQA, captioning, interleaved image-text) in the mixture instead of fine-tuning on robot data alone, which prevents catastrophic forgetting of web concepts. Robot data was re-weighted to roughly 50% (RT-2-PaLI-X) and 66% (RT-2-PaLM-E) of each batch.

Output constraint at decode time: when prompted with a robot-action task the vocabulary is restricted to valid action tokens only; on standard VLM tasks the full natural-language vocabulary remains available.

Backbones and scale: RT-2-PaLI-X from PaLI-X 5B and 55B (ViT-22B + 32B UL2-style encoder-decoder), RT-2-PaLM-E from PaLM-E 12B (decoder-only LLM + ViT-4B projector). Also a PaLI-3B variant for the simulated Language-Table benchmark.

Real-time inference constraint: 55B is too large for on-robot GPUs, so the model is served from a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network, reaching 1-3 Hz for 55B and ~5 Hz for the 5B / 3B variants. Authors flag inference cost as the main scaling bottleneck and point to quantization and distillation.

Results (6k real evaluation trials, 7-DoF mobile manipulator): matches RT-1 on seen tasks (~91-93% vs 92%) but roughly 2x better average on unseen objects/backgrounds/environments (62% vs 32% for RT-1, vs ~10-12% for VC-1/R3M), and >3x better on emergent symbol understanding, reasoning and person-recognition instructions (60% vs 17%).

Emergent capabilities come from transferred semantics, not new motor skills: following commands that were never in robot data ('move apple to 3', 'push coke can on top of heart'), spatial/relational reasoning ('cup with same color', 'sum of two plus one'), logos, nutrition priors, celebrity/person identification, and multilingual instructions.

Chain-of-thought variant: fine-tune a few hundred steps with an added 'Plan:' field before the action tokens ('Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: 1 128 124 ...'), which bridges VQA visual reasoning and manipulation data and enables multi-stage semantic inference (e.g. pick a rock as an improvised hammer).
Ablations: training from scratch is far worse (9% avg) than fine-tuning (42-52%) which is worse than co-fine-tuning (44-63%); larger models generalize better (55B co-fine-tune 63% vs 5B 44%).

Stated limitations: no new motions beyond the robot data distribution (7 skills: pick, move-near, place-upright, knock-over, open/close drawer, place-into-receptacle), poor at grasping by specific parts, dexterous/precise manipulation, and deep multi-layer reasoning; also high inference cost and few openly fine-tunable VLMs available at the time.

Practical read-across for reimplementation: the recipe is backbone-agnostic, so any image-text-to-text model with a large VLM pretraining corpus plus a discretized-action token vocabulary can be turned into a VLA.

name: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Model Design Pattern
observations: Unify language and control in a single token space: discretize continuous end-effector deltas into bins and emit them as ordinary text tokens so a pretrained VLM needs zero architectural changes.
Co-fine-tune rather than fine-tune: keep web VQA/captioning data in the batch mixture to preserve semantic generalization.
Constrain decoding to the action vocabulary only during robot prompts, while leaving full language ability intact for VQA prompts.
Treat serving infrastructure as part of the design: either shrink/distill the model or host it remotely and accept 1-5 Hz closed-loop control.
Optional chain-of-thought 'Plan' field before actions improves multi-step semantic reasoning.

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
observations: Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot (v0.6.1); end-to-end robot learning stack covering datasets, policies, training and evaluation, with a Hub-based dataset and checkpoint format.

Ships current VLA policies such as SmolVLA and pi0 alongside classic imitation-learning baselines like ACT and diffusion policy, so the RT-2 style workflow (pretrained VLM backbone fine-tuned on robot trajectories) is available without custom code.

CLI-driven workflow: `lerobot-train --policy.type=smolvla --policy.load_vlm_weights=true --dataset.repo_id=... --steps=... --batch_size=...`, with optional `--policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base` for fine-tuning a released checkpoint (e.g. 20k steps ~4h on a single A100).

Supports parameter-efficient adaptation of VLA policies via PEFT/LoRA flags (`--peft.method_type=LORA --peft.r=64 --peft.lora_alpha=64`), which is the practical answer to RT-2's compute-cost limitation.

Integrated simulators/benchmarks for closed-loop evaluation with `--env.type` (libero, libero_plus, robocasa) plus `--env_eval_freq`, `--eval.n_episodes`, mirroring RT-2's emphasis on quantitative rollout evaluation.
Chosen as the best current starting point for vision-language robotics workflows because it combines HF VLM checkpoints, dataset tooling, and real/sim robot control loops in one maintained project.

name: Hugging Face Transformers image-text-to-text APIs
observations: Context7 ID /huggingface/transformers; provides the VLM backbones (PaliGemma, SmolVLM, Qwen-VL, Idefics, LLaVA-family, etc.) that play the role PaLI-X/PaLM-E played in RT-2.

Standard fine-tuning path: AutoProcessor for image+text preprocessing, AutoModelForImageTextToText, and Trainer with `processing_class=processor` and a DataCollator; TrainingArguments covers bf16, gradient checkpointing, gradient accumulation and LR scheduling.

The official VQA/image-text-to-text task docs and TRL (SFTTrainer / VLM alignment) are the recommended route for supervised fine-tuning of vision-language models, which maps directly onto RT-2's VQA-format robot data.
Custom token vocabularies can be added or repurposed via the tokenizer, which is how the RT-2 'reserve 256 tokens as action bins' trick would be reproduced today.
